title: Burg Freundsberg Schwaz
highlights: Prominent landmark of the historic silver-mining town of Schwaz
Mighty five-story Romanesque keep originating from the 12th century
Museum of the City of Schwaz showcasing Tyrolean silver mining heritage
Castle tavern with a scenic panoramic terrace overlooking the Inn valley
kurzbeschreibung: Perched high above Schwaz, Burg Freundsberg houses the municipal museum dedicated to local mining history within its Romanesque keep.
beschreibung:
Landmark of Tirol's Silver City

Burg Freundsberg perches on a steep hill roughly 170 metres above the storied silver mining town of Schwaz. Built around 1170 by the Lords of Freundsberg (Herren von Freundsberg) as their ancestral seat, this fortified castle stands as a testament to the region's medieval significance.

Museum in the Romanesque Keep

The mighty five-storey keep houses the Museum der Stadt Schwaz. Beautifully curated exhibition rooms showcase the heyday of Tirol silver mining, the town's artistic heritage, and the prominent influence of the Fugger merchant dynasty. After touring the museum, the Burgschenke castle tavern invites guests to relax on its panoramic sun terrace overlooking the Inntal.
